name: testimonial
title: Testimonial
description: One customer quote with attribution, or a short grid of them.

frame.summary: A single quote is prose in a section. The multi-quote variant is a list grid; Card is only used if quotes become navigable case-study links.

components.name: text
components.for: Quote body (role large for a single quote) and attribution.

components.name: avatar
components.for: The person's photo or initials; decorative because the name is in the caption.

use: The level the surrounding page gives this block — a template passes it explicitly.
dont: Choosing a level for its visual size. Size is the Heading component's `role`, a separate decision.
headingLevel.a11y: No default, for the reason Heading's `level` has none: only the caller knows the depth, and a skipped level breaks heading navigation for the whole page.

title.summary: Optional section heading. Without it the block is a plain section with no landmark.

quotes.type: Array<{ quote: ReactNode; name: string; role?: string; company?: string; avatar?: string }>

decisions.why: Auto-advancing content needs pause controls (WCAG 2.2.2), hides most quotes from most readers, and this system has no carousel primitive. A grid of three shows more in less code.
The native pairing ties the attribution to the quote for assistive technology without ARIA.
The name is in the caption; Avatar's `decorative` prop exists for exactly this, so the name is not read twice.

landmarks.label: aria-labelledby the section heading — only when a title is given; otherwise no landmark

obligations: Quotes must be real and attributable; the block does not fabricate social proof.

native.reason: Website-only by decision B3 (gate-1 review, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md): marketing blocks and templates ship on the web only and get no native version. Marketing composition. A native app is reached after install, so there is nothing to persuade or convert; the equivalent content in-app is an onboarding or paywall screen, which is a different block with different obligations.

tokenGaps.need: A section-band vertical padding step larger than space.section for marketing rhythm
tokenGaps.interim: padding-block uses var(--rata-space-section) top and bottom. space.section is the only page-rhythm step and was sized for docs pages, not full-bleed marketing bands.

tokenGaps.need: A grid gutter role (column and row gap between tiles)
tokenGaps.interim: gap: var(--rata-space-gap-lg) between tiles, var(--rata-space-stack-lg) between rows when they wrap. space.gap.* is documented for inline items, not grid gutters.
